_comment: PNPT Configuration & Tracking source-of-truth. Phases describe the 5-stage PNPT methodology (Kickoff → Discovery → Build → Validate → Closeout) with an Initiation stage prepended for PM/PC system setup. Each package carries its own in-scope tool list, deliverable templates, and a configuration workbook structured exactly like the SPC's `PNPT Configuration Workbook _ NAMER.xlsx` (per-section settings with default, decision logic, and notes). Per-client progress is stored in localStorage.

phases.name: Initiation
phases.description: System setup, internal pit stop, and project resourcing kick off the moment the project is assigned. Critical: SPCs must be resourced same day so the 4-hour consultation blocks can be scheduled at the kickoff call.

tasks.text: Review project assignment in Certinia (budget, duration, package SKU)
Create project folder structure in the shared drive
Create the project Slack channel and pin Implementation Plan + RAID log
Set up Smartsheet workspace — Plan, Validation Script, RAID log only (3 sheets)
Update Outreach email templates for this package's touchpoints
Update Gong Brief targeted to package touchpoints
Run internal pit stop with AE / CSE / AM (commercial upmarket)
Resource the project — submit SPC request same day / next morning
Forecast the project in Certinia using the PNPT forecasting curve
Send welcome email and attach the package Slick
Customer self-paced: complete Procore Tool Certifications before discovery (front-loaded to accelerate configuration sessions)

phases.name: Kickoff
phases.description: Rebranded from the Alignment Call. Highly prescriptive — introduce the package journey, set scope and deliverable expectations, and schedule every meeting on the call (discovery, consultations, configuration training, validation Q&A, closeout) before the customer leaves.

tasks.text: Send kickoff invite via Outreach template (attach Slick + agenda)
Run the kickoff deck: Introductions (PM/PC, AM, CSE)
Walk through Support resource (turnaround, channels, scope vs PM/SPC)
Review certifications and call out which to prioritise pre-discovery
Walk through 3-tier Procore Committee (Exec Sponsor, Implementation Lead, Key Experts) + responsibilities
Confirm the Procore Committee names + Key Experts per tool
Run 'What We Heard' slide — Goals, Key Dates, Tools, Projects (debrief sales, do not re-interview)
Explain Procore default platform + SmoothX-style consulting overlay framing
Walk the 5-phase flywheel methodology
Walk timeline slide — call out deliverable touchpoints
Deep dive Scope & Deliverables for the package
Confirm in-scope vs self-guided tools (1:1 swaps OK, no scope additions)
Call out Definition of Done (scope + configs + validation = complete)
Introduce Project Plan + RAID log in Smartsheet
Schedule ALL meetings: discovery, consultations, configuration training, validation Q&A, closeout
Confirm pre-discovery action items (WBS, cost code list, forms, distribution)
Send follow-up email (Outreach template) + update RAID with any kickoff risks
Schedule PM/PC ↔ SPC delivery pit stop

phases.name: Discovery & Design
phases.description: SPC-led workshop that maps current state to desired state and surfaces foundational architecture. Replaces the old Account Configuration call — the SPC is now responsible for the company-level architecture decisions previously surfaced by PM/PC.

tasks.text: Run delivery pit stop with PM/PC before workshop — review 'What We Heard', budget, key risks, ProCore Committee, sales-side context
Discovery Workshop — Welcome: introduce Procore Delivery Team (SPCs) + capture attendees
Discovery Workshop — Alignment: identification of key stakeholders & decision makers
Discovery Workshop — Walk the Advise & Configure motion (Discovery → Configuration Sessions → Behind-the-scenes Configuration Work → Configuration Training → Q&A/Closeout)
Discovery Workshop — Company Setup & Workflows section: offices, business units, trades, departments, permission groups
Discovery Workshop — WBS / cost code structure (Standard vs custom segments, ERP-driven vs Procore-driven)
Discovery Workshop — Permissions architecture: role → template mapping, granular permission needs
Discovery Workshop — Process Flows: walk each in-scope tool's 'Diagrams' tab from its support article
Discovery Workshop — For each in-scope tool, capture current process and where the OOTB flow won't fit
Discovery Workshop — Introduce the custom fields & fieldsets concept; flag which tools will need them at configuration time
Discovery Workshop — Wrap with Current State + Desired State framing (run AI prompts against the Gong recording afterwards)
Build Discovery Workshop Summary deliverable (Current State + Desired State PDF) and send to customer
Provide pre-consultation homework (WBS / cost code list, forms, distribution lists, decisions)
Flag any gap risks to the RAID log — anything not covered by MVP scope

phases.name: Build (Consult + Configure)
phases.description: 4-hour consultation sessions paired with heads-down configuration. SPC walks the customer through tool overview → settings → permissions → templates/workflows → role-reversal sandbox, then configures the customer's Sandbox project and Standard Project Template. Every setting change is logged in the Configuration Workbook in real time.

tasks.text: Block configuration time on calendar (billable, client name, deliverable)
Stand up the Sandbox project for the customer to validate against
Per-tool consultation: Tool Overview (engine + custom fields)
Per-tool consultation: Project-level Settings + decisions
Per-tool consultation: Permissions confirmation + granular adjustments
Per-tool consultation: Templates + Workflows build (within package limits)
Per-tool consultation: Role-reversal — customer drives, SPC observes
Per-tool consultation: Workbook gap check before ending the call
Heads-down: Company Admin (general settings, trades, fieldsets)
Heads-down: Permissions templates (Company + Project)
Heads-down: Company-level templates (Inspections, Action Plans, Correspondence)
Heads-down: Workflows tool (max per package limit)
Heads-down: Standard Project Template — tool by tool
Heads-down: Custom fields / fieldsets per tool
Configuration Workbook: complete EVERY setting change in real time
Send weekly check-in (template) — track Plan + RAID with customer

phases.duration: 4 hours per tool-group consultation + ~2 hours heads-down configuration per group

phases.name: Validate
phases.description: Configuration Training plus the customer-led validation pass. Walk the company-admin / permissions / directory / templates / standard project template top-down, then hand off the Configuration Workbook + Validation Script and run a Product Q&A meeting to address any gaps before closeout.

tasks.text: Run Configuration Training: Company Admin tool overview + configured changes
Configuration Training: Permissions Templates overview + 4 access levels + granular
Configuration Training: Directory overview (NOT importing — customer or RAS owns this)
Configuration Training: Company-level templates review
Configuration Training: Workflows tool review
Configuration Training: Standard Project Template — tool by tool review
Send Outreach validation kickoff email with attached Configuration Workbook + Validation Script
Set the validation window expectation (short turnaround)
Run Product Q&A meeting(s) — address validation findings
Update Configuration Workbook with any post-validation tweaks
Confirm validation complete with customer in writing

phases.duration: Configuration Training: 1–2 hours (Enterprise may need 2× 2-hour blocks) + asynchronous customer testing + Product Q&A
phases.format: Customer training + customer-led validation + Q&A meeting

phases.name: Closeout
phases.description: Maps to the GPS deck "Go-Live" phase: customer goes live on projects, closeout deliverable produced, transition to CSE / Team. Definition of Done must be met before this phase opens.

tasks.text: Build the Project Closeout Document — pull Implementation Summary from Gong
Closeout Document: Key Configuration Achievements + Lessons Learned
Closeout Document: Definition of Done checklist (all green)
Closeout Document: Essential links (Plan, RAID, Workbook, Discovery deck, Validation script)
Closeout Document: Remaining Tasks + Remaining Risks (from Plan + RAID)
Closeout Document: Consultant Recommendations (betas, future SOW candidates)
Run knowledge transfer with CSE / AM / Renewals Manager — meeting or Slack summary
Schedule + run the Closeout Call with customer + CSE
Walk customer through the Closeout Deliverable and confirm Definition of Done
Value-prop CSAT survey on the call (mention follow-up midpoint + final surveys)
Close project in Certinia (timecards approved, budget reconciled)
Update Salesforce general notes + archive Smartsheet workspace
Remove project users from IPA / shared drive access list
Final Slack summary in account channel + share folder link

consultationShift.name: How Consultation Shifts — ACD vs PNPT
consultationShift.subtitle: Slides 40-41. The order and the SPC's authorship changes — tool drives scope, SPC physically configures.

buckets.name: Current State — Advise (ACD / SOW)
buckets.description: Cycle: Process → Tool Mapping → Advise. SPC provides recommendations and educates on the setting changes that need to take place in line with SOPs. Customer has ownership of seeing through process configurations and SOPs. Process-first leads to scope ambiguity and longer build cycles — a great fit for SOWs because the customer pays for that level of depth.

buckets.name: New State — Advise & Configure (PNPT)
buckets.description: Cycle: Tool → Process → Advise → Configure. The new packages start with the tool because the tool is what controls the scope. The SPC advises on the process nuances and then physically goes 'under the hood' to build the templates, workflows, and permissions for the client. The SPC is a strategic architect focused on MVP — depth of process is regulated by the tool scope. Driving decisions in real time to support configuration is critical.

talkTrackShifts.name: Talk Track Shifts
talkTrackShifts.subtitle: Slide 42. The ACD talk track centered on what the customer should change. The PNPT talk track centers on what the SPC is about to configure — and asks one nuance question per setting to drive the decision in real time.

examples.acd: "Here is my recommendation for this setting and this is where you should change your RFI configurations, like setting the default response time to 3 days."
examples.new: "I'm going to walk you through the standard lifecycle of an RFI in Procore. As you can see, the default gives reviewers 3 days to respond. Based on your process nuances, does that 3-day window work for your team, or do I need to adjust that default setting for you in the master template?"

examples.topic: Daily Log custom fieldsets / delay codes
examples.acd: "What are your current Daily Log processes, you can create a Custom Fieldset so you can add your own delay codes to the Daily Log."
examples.new: "What are your current Daily log processes? Based on that, are there any specific data points missing here that your executives need to see? Okay, you need to track specific weather delays. I will build a Custom Fieldset for your Delay Log to ensure that data is captured."

examples.acd: "What is your existing approval workflow. To create a workflow, you add a trigger here, and then you add steps. Do you want to try setting up a parallel or sequential routing logic for your invoices?"
